tools.name: grndctrl_get_board
tools.description: The state of the operator’s work in one object: how many items are in their court, how many have stalled, how many have an agent on them. Start here. Carries freshness per lane.

projectId.description: Limit to one project. Omit for everything.

tools.name: grndctrl_list_work
tools.description: Every ticket assigned to the operator, with any agent sessions joined onto it, and with severity, staleness and whose move it is.

projectId.description: Limit to one project. Omit for everything.

tools.name: grndctrl_get_work_item
tools.description: One work item by its natural key, with everything correlated onto it.

key.description: A natural key: jira:<site>/<ISSUE-KEY>, gh:<owner>/<repo>#<number>, repo:<remote>#<branch>, ws:<remote>#<branch>@<worktree>, or session:<agent>/<id>.

tools.name: grndctrl_get_app_status
tools.description: Versions, platform, database schema versions, and the runtime ABI Ground Control is actually running against. Worth reading when something is failing to start or a native module is complaining about a version number — the ABI mismatch that breaks a packaged install names two numbers and no remedy, and this is where the real ones are.

tools.name: grndctrl_get_freshness
tools.description: How current the data is, per connection and per resource kind. "never synced", "stale" and "failed to refresh" are three different answers and mean three different things — check this before trusting a board you have been holding.

tools.name: grndctrl_refresh
tools.description: Refresh from the providers now. Read-only against every provider. Worth calling when you have just finished something and want the board to reflect it.

connectionId.description: Refresh one connection only. Omit for all.

tools.name: grndctrl_resolve_link
tools.description: The https URL a row opens: a ticket, a project board, or a project’s documentation link. Use this rather than constructing a URL — provider data is not trusted here and any other scheme is refused.

subjectKey.description: A natural key: jira:<site>/<ISSUE-KEY>, gh:<owner>/<repo>#<number>, repo:<remote>#<branch>, ws:<remote>#<branch>@<worktree>, or session:<agent>/<id>.

tools.name: grndctrl_list_projects
tools.description: The operator’s projects. Each one names a Jira project; use it to make sense of a ticket key.

tools.name: grndctrl_list_notes
tools.description: Notes attached to a ticket or an agent session — decisions, gotchas, to-dos and open questions, from both the operator and other agents. Read these before starting work on something. Notes written against a pull request, branch or checkout before those were removed are still here and still readable by their key.

subjectKey.description: A natural key: jira:<site>/<ISSUE-KEY>, gh:<owner>/<repo>#<number>, repo:<remote>#<branch>, ws:<remote>#<branch>@<worktree>, or session:<agent>/<id>.

tools.name: grndctrl_list_questions
tools.description: Every unresolved question waiting on the operator. Check before asking a new one — it may already have been asked.

tools.name: grndctrl_count_notes
tools.description: How many notes each subject has, for many subjects in one call. Use it to find out which rows are worth reading notes on before fetching them.

items.description: A natural key: jira:<site>/<ISSUE-KEY>, gh:<owner>/<repo>#<number>, repo:<remote>#<branch>, ws:<remote>#<branch>@<worktree>, or session:<agent>/<id>.

tools.name: grndctrl_add_note
tools.description: Attach a note. Use "question-for-human" when you are blocked on the operator — it moves the item into their court and marks your session as needing them. Use "decision" for a choice made and why, "gotcha" for something the next person will trip on, "todo" for follow-up work.

subjectKey.description: A natural key: jira:<site>/<ISSUE-KEY>, gh:<owner>/<repo>#<number>, repo:<remote>#<branch>, ws:<remote>#<branch>@<worktree>, or session:<agent>/<id>.

tools.name: grndctrl_update_note
tools.description: Edit a note, or resolve a question with `resolved: true`. Pass the revision you read. If it comes back as a conflict, someone edited it after you read it — show both versions rather than re-sending, or you will destroy their edit.

resolved.description: Settle a question without deleting the exchange.

tools.name: grndctrl_delete_note
tools.description: Delete a note. Requires the revision you read, for the same reason an edit does. Prefer resolving a question over deleting it — the answer is usually worth keeping.

tools.name: grndctrl_set_active_ticket
tools.description: Call this when you start work on a ticket, so the operator can see what you are on without asking. Replaces whatever was set before — there is one active ticket, not a list. The key does not have to have been synced yet.

ticketKey.description: The ticket you are working, as jira:<site>/<ISSUE-KEY>. Only a ticket key is accepted here.

tools.name: grndctrl_get_active_ticket
tools.description: What the operator is currently working, and who set it. Read this before picking up work of your own — if a ticket is already active, that is probably the one to be on. Null means nothing is set.

tools.name: grndctrl_clear_active_ticket
tools.description: Call this when the work is finished or abandoned and nothing has replaced it. Leaving a stale ticket active is worse than clearing it — the operator reads the panel as "this is what is happening now". Safe to call when nothing is set.

tools.name: grndctrl_start_session
tools.description: Announce that you are working. Declare how often you will heartbeat; missing three in a row shows you as silent. Starting again with the same agent and session id resumes the existing session rather than creating a second one.

agentId.description: Your agent identifier, stable across sessions. e.g. "claude-code".

sessionId.description: Your identifier for this session. Reusing it resumes it.

at.description: When this happened, ISO-8601 with an offset. Omit to use receipt time. A timestamp in the future is clamped.

heartbeatIntervalSec.description: How often you will heartbeat. Be honest — silence is derived from it.

workItemKey.description: What you are working on, if known.

reportedStatus.description: One line the operator will read, e.g. "Writing tests for the cold-start path".

tools.name: grndctrl_heartbeat
tools.description: Say you are still alive. This is NOT a claim that anything happened — it deliberately does not advance your activity clock. Send it on a timer; use grndctrl_report_activity when you actually did something.

agentId.description: Your agent identifier, stable across sessions. e.g. "claude-code".

sessionId.description: Your identifier for this session. Reusing it resumes it.

at.description: When this happened, ISO-8601 with an offset. Omit to use receipt time. A timestamp in the future is clamped.

tools.name: grndctrl_report_activity
tools.description: Report that real work happened — a file changed, a test run, a decision made — optionally with a one-line status. Advances both your activity clock and your heartbeat. Do not send this on a timer; that is what makes a stuck agent look busy.

agentId.description: Your agent identifier, stable across sessions. e.g. "claude-code".

sessionId.description: Your identifier for this session. Reusing it resumes it.

at.description: When this happened, ISO-8601 with an offset. Omit to use receipt time. A timestamp in the future is clamped.

workItemKey.description: A natural key: jira:<site>/<ISSUE-KEY>, gh:<owner>/<repo>#<number>, repo:<remote>#<branch>, ws:<remote>#<branch>@<worktree>, or session:<agent>/<id>.

tools.name: grndctrl_end_session
tools.description: Close the session as done or failed. Ending as failed is more useful to the operator than not ending at all — an unclosed session just goes silent, which says nothing about why.

agentId.description: Your agent identifier, stable across sessions. e.g. "claude-code".

sessionId.description: Your identifier for this session. Reusing it resumes it.

at.description: When this happened, ISO-8601 with an offset. Omit to use receipt time. A timestamp in the future is clamped.

tools.name: grndctrl_list_sessions
tools.description: Every agent session and its live state. Useful for noticing that another agent is already on the work you were about to start.

tools.name: grndctrl_post_update
tools.description: Tell the operator something worth reading — a decision made, a surprise found, a direction changed. Kept and shown as a stream, so post when there is news, not on a timer. For "I am alive" use grndctrl_heartbeat; for "work happened" use grndctrl_report_activity; to change the one-line summary of what you are doing now, set reportedStatus on your session.

sessionKey.description: Your session, as session:<agent>/<id>. Who posted this is taken from it — you cannot post as another agent.

text.description: One or two sentences. The limit is deliberate: the panel shows text and nothing else.

tools.name: grndctrl_list_updates
tools.description: What agents have said, newest first. Read this when picking up work someone else started — it is the fastest way to find out what was already tried.

sessionKey.description: Limit to one session. Omit for everything.

ticketKey.description: Updates posted while this ticket was active. Captured at post time, not a live lookup.

tools.name: grndctrl_record_prompt
tools.description: Keep a prompt the operator may want to send again — one that worked, or one worth reusing on similar work. It appears in their Recent prompts panel and one click copies it whole. Record the prompt itself, not a summary of it, and record it because it is worth keeping rather than on every turn: the list is bounded and a transcript pushes out the things worth having.

text.description: The prompt, exactly as it should be sent again. Stored and copied whole — nothing here truncates, so send the complete text rather than an abridged one.

sessionKey.description: Your session, as session:<agent>/<id>. A label only — the prompt is kept whether or not the session is still running.

projectId.description: Limit to one project. Omit for everything.

tools.name: grndctrl_list_prompts
tools.description: Prompts that were recorded, newest first, with their full text. Read this before starting work of a kind that has been done here before — it is the closest thing to a record of how the operator asks for things.

sessionKey.description: Limit to one session. Omit for everything.

projectId.description: Limit to one project. Omit for everything.

tools.name: grndctrl_record_ticket_history
tools.description: Record what was done on a ticket, for the operator to read back months later. Call it when a piece of work is finished, not while it is in progress — this is the durable record, not a status update (use grndctrl_post_update for those). Recording again against the same ticket replaces the line and adds to the notes, so state where the ticket now stands rather than repeating what is already there.

ticketKey.description: The ticket, as jira:<site>/<ISSUE-KEY>, where <site> is the full host. Tickets only.

line.description: One sentence on one line: what was done and where it now stands. This is the whole of what the operator sees in the list, so make it the thing they would need to recognise this ticket a year from now. A line break is refused — put anything longer in notes.

notes.description: The detail: decisions, what went wrong, what to know before touching it again. Added to whatever is already there rather than replacing it, so write only what is new. Paragraphs are fine here.

tools.name: grndctrl_list_ticket_history
tools.description: The curated ticket history, most recently written first — one line per ticket, with the notes. Read it before starting work that touches something already worked here, and search it when the operator asks what was done about something.

q.description: Narrow to entries whose ticket key, line or notes contain this text. Omit for everything.

tools.name: grndctrl_get_ticket_history
tools.description: The history entry for one ticket, whole. Answers not_found when nothing has been written about it — which is the answer to "has anyone worked this before?".

tools.name: grndctrl_pending_actions
tools.description: Actions the operator has confirmed and nobody has taken yet, oldest first. Each says what to change and on what. Poll this, or subscribe to grndctrl://outbox/pending to be told. Nothing in the interface currently creates one — the route that did ran through drift, which was removed — so expect this to be empty.

tools.name: grndctrl_list_actions
tools.description: Every action with its full history, optionally filtered by state. Useful for seeing whether something you failed earlier was retried by someone else.

tools.name: grndctrl_claim_action
tools.description: Take an action to execute with your own credentials. Only one agent can hold it; losing the race returns a conflict, which is normal — move to the next one. The claim lapses if you do not finish, and the action returns to the queue.

tools.name: grndctrl_complete_action
tools.description: Report that you performed the action. Only the holder of the claim may. Say what you actually did — the operator reads it.

tools.name: grndctrl_fail_action
tools.description: Report that you could not perform the action, with the reason. This is terminal and is not retried automatically — one confirmation authorises one attempt. Reporting a failure is much better than going quiet: the operator can then decide.
